skill.name: research-storage
skill.description: Defines storage paths, naming rules, file templates, and lookup patterns for reusable dokhak research caches.
skill.summary: Standardize dokhak research cache files and section lookup workflows.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced templates, pseudo-code, and path examples in SKILL.md. No executable shell commands, obfuscated code, reconnaissance behavior, prompt injection, or unauthorized network behavior were found in the reviewed source.

static_findings.snippet: > Glob does NOT return directories. All patterns MUST end with a filename (e.g., `/research.md`).
> | `.research/sections/*9-1*/*` | ✅ Returns all files in matching dirs |
This catches slug variations like `Core-Concepts`, `core_concepts`, etc.
Used by `researcher` agent for path resolution:
| `.research/` directory missing | Auto-create on first write          |

content.value_statement: Research agents can create inconsistent cache paths, source files, and section records. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code shared conventions for storing and finding reusable research.
actual_capabilities: Defines the .research directory structure for init research and section research.
Specifies canonical section directory names with chapter, section, and slug rules.
Provides templates for summary.md, sources.md, and research.md files.
Documents multi-tier lookup rules for legacy or inconsistent section directory names.
Defines XML response formats for research results and directory resolution.
Guides agents on when to read, write, or leave research files unchanged.
limitations: It does not collect research or verify source quality by itself.
It is not designed for direct end-user invocation.
It relies on other agents to follow the documented naming rules.
It does not include executable validators or migration scripts.

use_cases.title: Store Initial Topic Research
use_cases.description: Create standard summary and source registry files under the init research directory.

use_cases.title: Reuse Section Research
use_cases.description: Find existing section research even when older directories use inconsistent naming.

use_cases.title: Read Verified Context
use_cases.description: Load saved research files without changing them during outline or draft generation.

prompt_templates.title: Save Init Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for storing broad topic research.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the research-storage conventions to save init research for this topic. Create the summary and sources files in the standard init location.

prompt_templates.title: Create Section Research Files
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for one chapter section.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use research-storage to build the canonical section path for chapter {chapter}, section {section}, and title {title}. Save research and sources using the documented templates.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Existing Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow for finding cached section research.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the multi-tier directory resolution rules from research-storage to check whether research already exists for this section before creating new files.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Research Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for partial research reuse.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use research-storage to inspect the existing section research, identify missing subtopics, and update only the files that need additional coverage.

output_examples.input: Store initial research for a new learning project.
output_examples.output: The agent creates an init summary file and an init sources file with key concepts, learning path, trends, and source reliability notes.

output_examples.input: Find research for chapter 1, section 2, Core Concepts.
output_examples.output: The agent checks the canonical path first, then tries documented legacy variations before deciding whether new research is needed.

output_examples.input: Prepare a writer agent to draft from saved research.
output_examples.output: The agent provides resolved research file paths and keeps the writer in read-only mode for those files.

best_practices: Normalize chapter, section, and title values before creating section directories.
Use the source registry template whenever research files cite external material.
Check existing research with the multi-tier lookup flow before starting new research.
anti_patterns: Do not create section directories with padded section numbers.
Do not rely on one simple path match when legacy names may exist.
Do not let consumer agents modify cached research files.

faq.question: What does this skill store?
faq.answer: It defines where agents should store research summaries, source registries, and section research files.

faq.question: Does this skill perform web research?
faq.answer: No. It only defines storage conventions and templates for agents that perform research elsewhere.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects Read, Write, and Glob access for locating and updating research files.

faq.question: Can writers modify research files?
faq.answer: No. The skill says writer and structure agents should read saved research without modifying it.

faq.question: How does it handle old directory names?
faq.answer: It documents a multi-tier lookup process that checks canonical and legacy path variations.

faq.question: Is it useful outside dokhak?
faq.answer: It can inform similar agent workflows, but its paths and agent names are tailored to dokhak projects.
